name: Amzn-User
follows_en: Partial, may not follow all robots.txt directives because actions can be user-initiated

ips.note: Amazon publishes the Amzn-User IP addresses on a web page that shows the list as JSON, and links it from the Amazonbot documentation page.

ua: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; Amzn-User/0.1) Chrome/W.X.Y.Z Safari/537.36
vendor_quote: Because actions taken by Amzn-User can be initiated by a user, it may not follow all robots.txt directives.
what_en: Amzn-User is an Amazon user agent that supports user actions, such as responding to Alexa queries that require up-to-date information. Amazon says that when a customer asks a question, Amzn-User may fetch live information from the web to provide accurate answers on the user's behalf. Amazon says it does not crawl content for generative AI model training.
block_en: Amazon says Amzn-User may not follow all robots.txt directives because its actions can be initiated by a user. Amazon also says each of its user agent settings (Amazonbot, Amzn-SearchBot, Amzn-User) is independent of the others and may take about 24 hours to reflect changes.
compare_en: Amzn-SearchBot is an automated crawler for Amazon search experiences that Amazon says respects robots.txt, while Amzn-User fetches live information when a customer asks and may not follow all directives.
notes: Page says 'Chrome/W.X.Y.Z' as a placeholder; kept verbatim. IP page (live-ip-addresses) is HTML wrapping a JSON list: 1023 entries with no CIDR mask (single addresses), creationTime 2025-11-04, per our parse; not stated in JSON fields because brief says no count for HTML.
answer_en: Amzn-User is the Amazon user agent that fetches live pages when a customer asks Alexa something that needs current information. Amazon says it does not crawl for generative AI training and may not follow all robots.txt directives, because the action is user-initiated. Amazonbot and Amzn-SearchBot are separate settings.
